newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRIC FUTURES DROP ON WEATHER, PHYSICALS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRIC FUTURES DROP ON WEATHER, PHYSICALS.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures dropped midday Wednesday, extending yesterday's losses, on bearish weather forecasts and lower western physical power prices.
The complex appeared overvalued in relations with falling cash prices and moderate air-conditioning demand due to mild weather across the West, brokers and traders said.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona fell to $30.00-34.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), while those at the California-Oregon Border (COB) eased to $20.00-21.00.
"It looks kind of heavy because of the cooler weather," a Houston futures trader said.
Forecasters called for cool, dry weather in the northern section of the Southwest the rest of week and seasonal conditions in the rest of the region with chance of rain and thunderstorm.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures would run as low as 12 degrees F below normal in the interior area, while those along the coast would average near to slightly above normal.
As of 1243 EDT, September PV futures were down 76 cents at $29.75 a MWh after hitting a low at $29.30.
October PV fell 59 cents to $22.90. November PV lost 74 cents at $22.10.
September COB was down 10 cents at $23.00, trimming a 60 cent loss.
October COB slipped 65 cents at $22.15. November COB traded 30 cents lower to $23.00.
In generation news, power production at the 1,139 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state was reduced briefly because an adjustable speed drive for a recirculation pump malfunctioned.
A 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired plant in Washington state was expected to be back on line today after shutting Monday for repairs.
Restart of the 750 MW unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was delayed to Tuesday afternoon due to a boiler tube leak.
The unit, which was shut over the weekend for repairs, had been expected to restart late Monday.
The 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was also scheduled to restart Tuesday afternoon after being shut Friday for unplanned repairs.
Separately, southbound transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie will be cut by 350 MW to 850 MW during certain hours today, according to the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
NYMEX estimated 179 COB and 261 PV contracts were sold as of midday Wednesday.
